subject: Acme renewal + expansion recap — usage, pain, next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@acme.com>, Samantha Lee <samantha.lee@acme.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 15 Sep 2026 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Acme renewal + expansion recap — usage, pain, next steps

Hi Alex / Samantha —

Thanks again for taking the time today. Wanted to capture the main points from our call and make sure we’re aligned on next steps. I’ve included Rishi and Neha for visibility on pricing and onboarding.

Summary (bulleted):
- Current state: Acme is on Redwood Hosted API (pay-as-you-go). Q2 usage ~ 1.1B tokens (see attached acme-q2-usage.csv).
- Pain points:
  - Increasing tail latency during peak batch inference for recommendations (~95th pct spikes to 700ms).
  - Rising token costs as new prompt templates rolled out; want better predictability.
  - Need for better observability on per-route cost and per-user quotas for internal finance.
- Goals:
  - Reduce tail latency and provide a predictable cost model for the new recommendation workload.
  - Support a higher concurrency pilot for new prompt variants (50–100 RPS sustained).
  - Keep data controls and audit logs for compliance.
- Proposed path: Pilot Dedicated Reserved Capacity (1x GPU pool) for recommendations in Oct -> expand to dedicated pool for production in Jan 2027. Pricing model: monthly reserved capacity + overage; Rishi to share ballpark numbers.

Attachments: Acme-MAP-v2.pdf (mutual action plan), acme-q2-usage.csv (usage export).

Open items / next steps:
1) Rishi: share a preliminary pricing estimate and optional quantization profile impact on latency by EOD Thu (2026-09-17).
2) Marissa (me): update the MAP with pilot scope and dates (attached).
3) Alex / Samantha: confirm any additional security requirements beyond SOC2 (e.g., custom KMS, IP allowlist) by Fri 2026-09-18.
4) Neha: prep SSO / SAML checklist and onboarding runbook for pilot.

If that looks right I’ll lock the pilot dates and push a short SOW draft.

Thanks —
Marissa Cole
Account Exec, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0123

--
Attachment(s): Acme-MAP-v2.pdf (12 pages)
Attachment(s): acme-q2-usage.csv (CSV, 1.2 MB)

From: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@acme.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Samantha Lee <samantha.lee@acme.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 15 Sep 2026 16:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Acme renewal + expansion recap — usage, pain, next steps

Thanks Marissa — this looks good and captures the conversation. A few clarifications from our side: 

- For latency: the 95th spikes are mostly on the recommendations endpoint (rec-v2); they coincide with batch jobs from our analytics pipeline between 10–11am PT. Can the pilot include a KV-cache warmup strategy to avoid cold-start spikes?
- For predictability: we like the reserved capacity model but need a clear overage cap or trigger for finance review. Can Rishi flag an overage threshold?
- Security: we will likely require customer-managed KMS for keys and an IP allowlist for the pilot; I’ll confirm exact requirements with our security team by Friday.

Next steps from Acme: Samantha will gather the security requirements and I’ll follow up with a draft timeline for our pilot engineering resources.

Appreciate the quick MAP — please send SOW when you have a pilot scope.

Best,
Alex
Alex Johnson
Head of Platform Engineering, Acme Corporation
alex.johnson@acme.com | (212) 555-0199

Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 15 Sep 2026 18:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Acme renewal + expansion recap — usage, pain, next steps

Alex —

Thanks for the quick note and the details. Short replies inline: 

- KV-cache warmup: yes — we’ll include a KV warmup + prefix caching strategy in the pilot runbook. Neha will own the runbook and steps to validate warmup.
- Overage cap: Rishi — can you propose 2 overage guardrails (soft alert threshold at 10% and hard cap with finance approval at 25%)? That would give Acme budget predictability.
- KMS / IP allowlist: noted. Samantha — if you can share the security requirements doc by Fri, we’ll route to our Private deployment team for feasibility and timeline.

I’ve attached an updated MAP (Acme-MAP-v2.pdf) with pilot dates: 2026-10-11 through 2026-10-29 (2-week pilot + 1-week observation). Proposed production go-live: 2027-01-10.

Next actions (owners & dates):
- Rishi: pricing + overage guardrail by 2026-09-17.
- Neha: onboarding runbook + KV warmup plan by 2026-09-24.
- Alex / Samantha: security requirements by 2026-09-18.
- Marissa: SOW draft and pilot SLOs by 2026-09-20.

Happy to hop on a quick follow-up if it helps — I can schedule a 30-min alignment next week.

-Marissa

--
Attachment(s): Acme-MAP-v2.pdf (updated 2026-09-15)
